motion: Clean energy can drive America's economic recovery.

dropped_turns.speaker: PRO
dropped_turns.text: Your worker-protection question assumes upgrades must force closure, and that premise is false. Sensible financing and phased work retain staff while cleaner investments create demand, so clean energy drives recovery.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Welcome. The motion is that clean energy can drive America's economic recovery. Danny argues for it, and Jillian argues against it. Each opening lasts thirty seconds, followed by two and a half minutes of crossfire and thirty-second closings. Speak directly, stay on the motion, let each other finish, and I will give a ten-second cue.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Recovery needs work that begins now and keeps paying back. Building cleaner power, upgrading homes, and making equipment create jobs while lowering bills. Those savings leave families and local businesses able to hire, spend, and grow, instead of sending money away for wasteful fuel. That's all, thank you.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Thank you, Danny. And that is the motion, clean energy can drive America's economic recovery today. And here to argue against the motion, Jillian.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: New projects can create work, but recovery needs dependable gains. If families face higher upfront bills, promised savings do not rescue budgets already under pressure.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: But you ignore the workers whose old jobs-

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Let her answer that.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: those people need steady paychecks, not promises that new industries may eventually replace them. Recovery means broad, reliable work, not a costly bet for communities.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: You've got ten seconds.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: A plan that raises risk for households cannot drive a durable, broad recovery at all. That's all, thank you.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Now we go on to round two. And round two is where the debaters address one another directly. You have two and a half minutes, starting when I stop talking.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: I agree cleaner equipment can lower a bill after installation. But the main question is whether it drives recovery, and costly transitions can drain households before benefits arrive.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: When financing is affordable and predictable, clean energy drives recovery by putting installers and suppliers to work. Those workers earn, spend, and support nearby businesses.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Your affordable financing point assumes someone else absorbs the risk. If projects fail to deliver savings, taxpayers or customers carry the loss, so recovery is not driven by clean energy.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: No, taxpayers need not carry losses when contracts require performance. You focus on failed projects, but reliable clean power protects firms from sudden fuel costs and supports recovery.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Clean energy projects should always pay for themselves. A recovery cannot rest on ventures that demand public support while families are already struggling.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Consider a workshop that installs efficient cooling and cleaner power, then uses lower monthly costs to keep its staff and buy materials. That direct local benefit proves clean energy can drive recovery.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: This clean energy project should not pay for itself. A community may support a project that protects a favorite view, but that choice shows why clean energy cannot drive economic recovery.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: You're saying clean energy projects should always pay for themselves but you still want this clean energy project should not pay for itself.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: The first statement concerns economic projects; the second describes a public choice with no economic purpose. Supporting an amenity can be worthwhile, yet it confirms clean energy is not a recovery engine.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Clean energy can strengthen recovery across many kinds of communities, from makers to renters. Its value is not limited to any single financing plan, because workable paths can lower costs.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: No, several paths do not make the overall gamble safe. Your claim ignores families facing price increases when projects need support, and those burdens can spread through-

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: That is exactly the problem with calling every investment a burden. A home repair crew sealing drafty rooms earns wages now, and residents keep more pay: recovery driven by clean energy.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Imagine a small manufacturer required to replace working machines before it can afford them. It cuts shifts to cover the expense, showing clean energy rules can slow recovery rather than drive it.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: That manufacturer deserves a practical timetable, not a sudden mandate. Yet the main issue is opportunity: cleaner upgrades create demand for builders, repair crews, and suppliers, driving recovery.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: About ten seconds left in the crossfire.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: If clean energy is the driver, how do you protect workers when-

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: And that's time. Now, we move on to round three, and round three are closing statements by each debater in turn. And making his closing statement, Danny.

turns.speaker: PRO
turns.text: Jillian's strongest point is that a costly change can hurt a fragile business. That risk calls for practical financing, not abandonment. Clean energy creates work, reduces recurring costs, and gives businesses steadier footing, so it can drive America's recovery. That's all, thank you.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Jillian, take the response.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Deciding this motion turns on more than whether a few projects create jobs. It turns on whether clean energy is reliable enough to lead the whole recovery without shifting heavy costs onto households and employers. Danny offers safeguards, but safeguards admit the plan can strain those already trying to stay open. A driver must pull everyone forward.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: I can give you ten seconds to do this.

turns.speaker: CON
turns.text: Clean energy may help, but the motion says it can drive recovery. When success depends on subsidies, timing, and firms absorbing changes, it is not the engine described. Recovery needs dependable-

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: I have to step in because we hit our time limit.

turns.speaker: MOD
turns.text: Thank you, Danny and Jillian, for a direct debate on the motion. This concludes our discussion here today.
